# Installing the tools {#sec-installation}

## No installation: BNG Playground

[BNG Playground](https://ruleworld.github.io/bngplayground/) runs BioNetGen in
a web browser. Paste any model from this book into its editor and click
**Run**. It is the quickest way to try a model, and it works on any computer.

## Visual Studio Code

1. Install [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com).
2. In the Extensions panel, search for **BioNetGen** and install it.
3. Open a `.bngl` file and click the run button in the editor toolbar. Results
   are written to a time-stamped folder and the main output (`.gdat`) opens in
   a plot viewer.

The extension needs Python and Perl. It installs PyBioNetGen, which contains
BioNetGen itself, when first used. macOS and Linux include Perl. On Windows,
install [Strawberry Perl](https://strawberryperl.com).

To keep results out of your working folders, set
`bngl.general.result_folder` in VS Code's settings to an absolute path, for
example a `BNG-results` folder in your project.

## Python

The book's Python code uses three packages:

- [bngsim](https://bngsim.readthedocs.io): fast ODE and stochastic simulation
  of BioNetGen models, run in-process from Python.
- [PyBioNetGen](https://pybionetgen.readthedocs.io): supplies BioNetGen, which
  bngsim uses to turn a `.bngl` file into a reaction network.
- `numpy`, `pandas`, and `matplotlib` for analysis and plotting.

Install them with

```bash
pip install bngsim bionetgen numpy pandas matplotlib jupyter
```

or create the environment used to build this book:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate bionetgen-book
```

Check the installation by simulating the first model of @sec-reaction-networks:

```python
import bngsim
model = bngsim.Model.from_bngl("models/ch01/stat_step1_binding.bngl")
sim = bngsim.Simulator(model, method="ode")
model.reset()
result = sim.run(t_span=(0, 20), n_points=101)
print(result.observables["LR"][-1])   # about 0.989
```
